name: Tip Top Tea Shop
signature_dish: honey ginger lemon tea with bun omelette
why_it_matters: One of the original Char Dukan shops on the parade ground beside St Paul's Church (consecrated 1840). Operating for over 50 years, it's where Landour's hill regulars and trekking-down Mussoorie crowds intersect over honey-ginger-lemon tea.
insider_tip: The bun omelette is the local order, not the Maggi. Sit on the low parapet wall facing the church — the morning light there is what people actually come back for.
signature_address: 305-6, Char Dukan, Luxmanpuri, Rajmandi, Landour, Mussoorie 248179

name: Anil's Cafe
why_it_matters: The Char Dukan shop celebrities check into when they come to Landour — Sachin Tendulkar's endorsement is on the wall. Operating 50+ years, the pancakes here are why Landour residents bother walking up from the bazaar.
insider_tip: Skip the pancake queue at peak hours; the chai-and-pakoda crowd at the next bench moves twice as fast and gets you the same parade-ground view.
signature_address: Char Dukan, Rajmandi, Landour Cantonment, Mussoorie 248179

name: Cafe De Landour
why_it_matters: The newer addition that pushed Char Dukan past four shops. Live music in the evenings and a balcony hung over the Doon valley make it the date-night choice for Mussoorie weekenders.
insider_tip: Book the corner balcony table at sunset for the long valley line — the cafe has valet parking right at the door, rare for Landour where most places need a 200m walk.
signature_address: Char Dukan, near SBI ATM, Landour Cantonment, Mussoorie 248179

name: Doma's Inn
why_it_matters: Built from the ground up by Doma, the family's matriarch who arrived in Landour selling Tibetan thangkas roadside in the late 1940s. The kitchen still works to authentic Tibetan-Bhutanese-Burmese recipes — not the North Indian version of momos. Ruskin Bond's house shares a wall with one of the rooms.
insider_tip: Order the phaley (Tibetan stuffed bread) and the Bhutanese ema datshi — the menu is huge but those two are what set Doma's apart from any North Indian Tibetan place.
signature_address: Char Dukan Road, Landour Cantonment, Mussoorie 248179

name: Landour Bakehouse
why_it_matters: Mars Hospitality (Sanjay & Rachna Narang) rebuilt the bakery using recipes from the 1900s Landour Cookbook — a community-club volume started by Mrs Lucas (Kellogg Church pastor's wife) and Irene Parker. Most desserts are still named after the original contributors. The art deco interior is designed to look like a 19th-century kitchen.
insider_tip: Sister's Bazaar gets its name from the British Military Hospital nurses who lived here from the 1820s onward. Combine the bakehouse with a 10-minute walk to Prakash's General Store across the road for cheese, peanut butter and jam.

name: Emily's
why_it_matters: Inside Rokeby Manor (built 1840, named after Walter Scott's poem) and named for Emily Eden, the Raj-era memoirist who wrote in Landour. Designed as an English tea room on the first floor, with Garhwali kafuli served alongside continental mains — one of the few Landour kitchens that takes the local cuisine seriously.
insider_tip: Afternoon tea on the verandah is the underused booking — most people come for dinner. The valley line at 4pm reads better than any night view here.

name: Cafe Ivy (Devdar Woods)
why_it_matters: Heritage Lal Kothi guesthouse on Chukkar Road, 100m from Sister's Bazaar — main building is a restored British-era guesthouse preserved by the Prakash family. The lawn sits under a 150-250 year-old deodar tree. Now run by Amarjeet & Sunita Kudle of La Villa Bethany; rebranded from Cafe Ivy to Devdar Woods Cafe.
insider_tip: Lawn seating fills first; the indoor lounge with the fireplace is the better cold-weather spot and most tourists miss it. Walk the Chukkar (Landour's 3km loop trail) starting from here.
signature_address: Chukkar Road, near Sister's Bazaar, Landour Cantonment, Mussoorie 248179

name: Char Dukan Cafe
why_it_matters: The recycled-wood reboot of the Char Dukan strip — minimalist, designed-for-Instagram, with a working fireplace and a small valley-view balcony. Sits beside Tip Top and Anil's, but reads completely modern; the contrast is the point.
insider_tip: Order at the counter and grab the balcony bench before the table service starts; their kitchen is small and the wait stretches in peak season.
signature_address: Char Dukan, Rajmandi, Landour Cantonment, Mussoorie 248179
